title: $\gamma_d$ is surjective for $d\geq g$
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] which is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], of genus $g=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-genus]. For $d\in\mathbf Z$ let $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ be the subfunctor of the Picard functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ [def-pc-picard-functor] on $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ of the classes whose fibrewise degree [def-pd-fibrewise-degree] is identically $d$. Let $d\geq g$, let $H_d$ be a $k$-scheme representing $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor], let $P_d$ be a $k$-scheme representing $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, and let $\gamma_d:H_d\to P_d$ be the morphism $D\mapsto\mathcal O(D)$ of [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism]. Then $\gamma_d$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), clause (5) 'the morphisms gamma_d are surjective for d >= g', and its proof, fourth paragraph: 'Let d >= g. Then for any field extension K/k and any invertible O_{X_K}-module L of degree d, chi(X_K, L) = d+1-g > 0. Hence L has a nonzero section and we conclude that L = O_{X_K}(D) for some divisor D of degree d. It follows that gamma_d is surjective'
